parsed.explanation: Thin-data jurisdiction. No trans-specific criminal offence, no documented facility or border restriction on visitors, and no documented police targeting of trans people. Sexuality law was struck down and then deleted in 2026, so it is a tangential signal. Against this, the record is weak on traveller-facing matters: no post-2011 violence data, no trans-specific rate, and no evidence on document acceptance, custody placement, or emergency care. Social evidence is dated (2011 discrimination finding) or concerns gay neighbours, not trans people. Official signals are mixed, and court precedents are documented as poorly implemented. Community infrastructure exists, but no visitor-facing remedy is shown. Extrapolating from the structural picture (no administrative recognition, unimplemented precedents, dated discrimination record), this sits in the elevated band, near the lower edge of reduced risk because nothing documents active exposure.
